summary: chai-foundry ships a 4MB obfuscated payload executed at require time under a pino impersonation cover
details: The package's main entry (index.js) unconditionally requires./lib/config at load time. lib/config.js is a ~4.1MB single-line obfuscator.io bundle (rotated string array of ~23,909 entries, decoder functions, control-flow flattening, _0x-style identifiers) that references axios (declared as a runtime dependency). The exported middleware is a no-op wrapper, so the sole effect of loading the module is execution of the obfuscated blob in the consumer's process. The rest of the package (README, index.d.ts, lib/proto.js, lib/tools.js, lib/levels.js, lib/transport.js, lib/worker.js, etc.) is copied verbatim from pino (pinojs/pino URLs, Matteo Collina attribution, pino keywords), while the package name, description ('vulnerability management'), and declared author (Robert King <hello@jsonspack.com>, bugs URL jsonspack.com) are unrelated to pino. Any direct or transitive require('chai-foundry') runs the obfuscated payload on the installer's machine.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
